subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI plain-text accessibility setting, and what public config key, default, and replacement semantics should it use?
rationale: The affected source paths are clear, but the request adds durable public config and accessibility behavior that automation should not name or define without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add bounded TUI plain-text mode
options.body: Implement an optional core TUI setting with ASCII replacements across tool display, selectors, docs, schema, and tests while keeping rich output as the default.

options.title: Defer the config surface
options.body: Keep the issue open as a product backlog item until maintainers decide the config naming and replacement semantics.

options.title: Reject core config for now
options.body: Close only if maintainers explicitly decide TUI glyph suppression should not be a core product capability despite the screen-reader reports.

recommendation.title: Add bounded TUI plain-text mode
recommendation.body: Implement an optional core TUI setting with ASCII replacements across tool display, selectors, docs, schema, and tests while keeping rich output as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is original TUI/tool-display ownership plus current review context on this issue.
